testsActuallyExecuted.note: All existing, written tests genuinely pass. The verdict below is about tests that were NEVER WRITTEN for spec-required proof obligations, and one control-flow bug the missing test would have caught, not about any failing test.

findings.summary: post_reel.py's shared finally: block unconditionally fires on every early return inside try:, including verify-only (:121) and DRY-ok (:181) -- both explicitly declared 'out of scope for the outcome vocabulary' by the spec's own Ground Truth section. This double-prints JSON on all 9 early-return paths and injects an unwanted outcome:"failed" key into the two non-failure paths, directly contradicting PROP-004(c)(iii)'s literal test assertion. Low production impact today (both real consumers read only the last stdout line and only fields unaffected by the leak), but a genuine, concretely-evidenced spec deviation.

A pending-verify clip whose sidecar is valid but whose .txt caption is ALSO missing crashes post_reel.py silently (caption file opened outside any try/except) -- self_heal.py accidentally stays safe via a 3-layer chain of exception-swallowing, but this is undesigned, unlogged, and completely untested.

PROP-004(c) (dry-mode zero-regression), PROP-006(b) (hook-collision/different-token regression), PROP-006(c)'s corrupt-JSON-sidecar sub-case, and PROP-011's 3-outcome temp-file-cleanup assertion are all explicitly 'Required (lean): true' in the approved spec but have ZERO corresponding tests. One of the four (PROP-004(c)) would have caught a real bug (FIND-100) had it been written; the other three guard correct-but-unverified code.

self_heal.py's actual __main__ CLI entrypoint (what run.sh really invokes) re-derives the ANICCA_INSTANCE path-suffix convention independently in Python instead of receiving it from the canonical _instance_paths.sh (which run.sh has already sourced moments earlier in the same script). Correct today, but an unenforced duplication with zero test coverage of the entrypoint itself -- test_self_heal.py only exercises run_self_heal() directly, bypassing __main__.

positiveFindings: reel_verify.py's 4 pure functions (_reads_stable, stabilize_reads, diff_new_href, classify_outcome, select_confirmed_href) are genuinely singly-defined in one shared module and imported (not reimplemented) by both post_reel.py and post_reel.py's caller chain -- no drift, matching the Gate's explicit 'no duplicate implementation' criterion for these specific functions.

REQ-001/002's exact 3-read/2-pair stabilize model is implemented correctly and matches PROP-001/002's fixtures exactly (independently re-derived by hand: reads=[[a],[a,b],[a,b]] -> stable via read2==read3; reads=[[a],[b],[c]] -> inconclusive, hrefs=None not last-read).

REQ-003's classify_outcome correctly requires BOTH candidate-present-on-reconfirm AND exact count+1 -- independently re-derived classify_outcome("X",["X","a"],2) by hand and confirmed it correctly returns unverified (count 2 != 2+1) despite candidate X being present, matching PROP-003's specific regression intent.

All 6 documented pre-share failure sites (:95,108,127,134,141,163) plus the new before-unstable-abort site correctly set outcome="failed" inline; classify_outcome is genuinely the ONLY site that can produce outcome="published" (confirmed via full control-flow read of post_reel.py's post-share branch).

REQ-010's token generation is confirmed to happen at exactly one site (run.sh:116, via secrets.token_hex(5)); self_heal.py never generates/derives a token, only reads sidecar["token"] -- confirmed via grep across both files.

$CAP is confirmed read-only across a real post attempt (test_prop011 empirically re-run: byte-identical content before/after); the mktemp+trap EXIT cleanup mechanism was empirically re-verified independently (0 leaked /tmp/clip-cap-* files before and after a real run), even though no test asserts this for all 3 outcomes (see FIND-102).

REQ-009's count_posts.py hand-verified against the real frozen 4-line fixture: dedup by URL correctly collapses lines 2+3 (identical DaLKV2xP8Ij) to count 2, matching the documented real-world incident math exactly. Fixture is genuinely committed to the anicca repo (git log confirms commit 9b47b31).

run.sh's IFS=$'\x1f' field-splitting was independently stress-tested with a URL containing query-string special characters and an href containing a literal space -- both round-tripped correctly through the JSON/shell boundary.

REQ-008's round-robin (oldest clip-file mtime) and REQ-006's clip+caption move-together were both independently hand-verified against their own test fixtures and additionally confirmed correct against a manually-traced trace of self_heal.py's control flow, not merely 'tests pass'.
All 30 existing tests (24 python unit/integration + 6 shell integration scripts) were actually executed in this review and genuinely pass -- no test failures found anywhere in the existing suite.
rationale: The core algorithmic implementation of this feature -- the race-free stabilize model, the outcome classification, the 3-way run.sh routing, the token-based self-heal confirmation, the round-robin fairness, and the URL-deduplicated monitor count -- is genuinely solid: independently re-derived by hand against multiple fixtures (not just 'tests pass'), and matches the approved spec's REQ-001 through REQ-010 with only one narrow, well-evidenced deviation (FIND-100). However, per the Gate's own requirement that Phase 3 confirm PROP-001..007 and PROP-009 PASS via a full control-flow read (not grep), that same control-flow read surfaced a real, concrete bug in post_reel.py's finally-block scope (FIND-100) that directly violates the spec's own explicit 'out of scope for the outcome vocabulary' carve-out and its own PROP-004(c) test requirement. Combined with three explicitly 'Required: true' proof obligations that were never implemented as tests (FIND-102, one of which would have caught FIND-100), one narrow but real cross-language logic duplication with zero test coverage of its actual entrypoint (FIND-103), and one edge case whose safety is accidental rather than designed and entirely untested (FIND-101), all five review dimensions have at least one concrete, citable, blocking finding. This sprint should route FIND-100 to a fix (scope the finally's setdefault+print to only fire when outcome is not already 'complete' for a non-failure path, or split verify-only/DRY-ok returns to fully bypass the shared finally's print), add the four missing tests named in FIND-102, add a test for FIND-101's missing-caption scenario (even if only to document the accidental-safety behavior as intentional), and either pass the already-resolved _instance_paths.sh values into self_heal.py's CLI wrapper as arguments or add a dedicated subprocess-level test asserting the wrapper's path derivation matches _instance_paths.sh (FIND-103) before Phase 3 can PASS.
